2-1.title: States of Matter
2-1.learn:
KEY IDEAS

Matter usually exists in three states, and the difference is all about how the tiny particles are arranged and how they move:
- Solid: particles are packed tightly and only vibrate in place. A solid keeps its OWN shape and volume.
- Liquid: particles are close but can slide past each other. A liquid keeps its volume but takes the SHAPE of its container and can flow.
- Gas: particles are far apart and zoom around freely. A gas spreads out to FILL any container, taking its shape and volume.

Example 1 — Shape and container
A rock (solid) keeps its shape on a table. Juice (liquid) takes the shape of the cup. Air (gas) fills the whole room.

Example 2 — Particle motion
In a solid, particles only vibrate. In a liquid, they slide. In a gas, they fly far apart and fast. More particle movement and spacing means a less rigid state.

Example 3 — Same substance, three states
Water can be ice (solid), liquid water (liquid), or water vapor (gas). It is the same substance — only the arrangement and motion of the particles differ.

questions.question: In which state of matter are particles packed tightly and only vibrate in place?
questions.explanation: In a solid, particles are tightly packed and only vibrate in place, so a solid keeps its shape.

questions.question: A substance that takes the shape of its container but keeps its own volume is a
questions.explanation: A liquid keeps its volume but flows to take the shape of its container.

questions.question: Which state of matter spreads out to fill any container it is in?
questions.explanation: Gas particles spread far apart and zoom around, so a gas fills the entire container.

questions.question: Which best describes the particles in a gas?

choices.A: Packed tightly and vibrating in place
choices.B: Close together but sliding past each other
choices.C: Far apart and moving around freely
choices.D: Locked together and unable to move

questions.explanation: Gas particles are far apart and move around freely and fast.

questions.question: Why does a solid keep its shape?

choices.B: Its particles are packed tightly and only vibrate in place

questions.explanation: Because the particles in a solid are tightly packed and only vibrate in place, the solid holds its shape.

questions.question: Juice poured into a glass takes the shape of the glass. This shows that juice is a
questions.explanation: A liquid flows and takes the shape of its container while keeping its volume.

questions.question: Which list correctly orders the states from most tightly packed particles to most spread out?
questions.explanation: Solids have the tightest packing, liquids are in between, and gases are the most spread out.

questions.question: Ice, liquid water, and water vapor are all water. What is different among them?

choices.B: The arrangement and motion of their particles

questions.explanation: All three are the same substance (water); only the arrangement and motion of the particles differ.

questions.question: A balloon filled with helium shows that a gas

choices.A: keeps a fixed shape on its own
choices.B: fills and takes the shape of its container

questions.explanation: The helium gas spreads out to fill the balloon and takes its shape, showing gas fills its container.

questions.question: Which statement about liquids and gases is TRUE?

choices.B: Both have particles that can move past each other, but gas particles are much farther apart
choices.C: Both have tightly packed, vibrating particles

questions.explanation: In both liquids and gases the particles can move past each other, but gas particles are much farther apart than liquid particles.

questions.question: Which state of matter keeps both its own shape AND its own volume?
questions.explanation: A solid keeps both its own shape and its own volume because its particles are locked tightly in place.

questions.question: In which state can particles slide past each other but still stay close together?
questions.explanation: In a liquid the particles stay close together but can slide past one another, which lets a liquid flow.

questions.question: A wooden block sits on a desk and keeps its exact shape. The block is a
questions.explanation: Because the block keeps its own shape, it is a solid; its particles are packed tightly and only vibrate in place.

questions.question: Air spreading out to fill an entire empty room is an example of a
questions.explanation: Air is a gas, and a gas spreads out to fill any container, taking its shape and volume.

questions.question: What two things change among the three states of matter?

choices.A: The arrangement of the particles and how they move
choices.B: The color and the smell of the particles

questions.explanation: The states of matter differ in how the particles are arranged and how they move, not in the substance itself.

questions.question: Milk poured from a jug into a bowl takes the shape of the bowl but its amount stays the same. This shows milk is a
questions.explanation: Milk keeps its volume but takes the shape of its container, which is the behavior of a liquid.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT a property of a solid?

choices.D: It spreads out to fill any container

questions.explanation: Spreading out to fill any container is a property of a gas, not a solid. A solid keeps its own shape and volume.

questions.question: Compared to a solid, the particles in a liquid are

choices.B: able to slide past each other
choices.C: locked in place and vibrating only
choices.D: completely separated and zooming far apart

questions.explanation: Liquid particles are close together like a solid's but, unlike a solid's, they can slide past each other so the liquid can flow.

questions.question: Which correctly matches a state to its particle motion?

choices.B: Liquid — particles only vibrate in place
choices.D: Gas — particles are locked in place

questions.explanation: In a gas the particles zoom around freely and are far apart, which matches the gas state.

questions.question: Why can a liquid flow but a solid cannot?

choices.B: A liquid's particles can slide past each other while a solid's only vibrate in place
choices.C: A solid's particles are farther apart

questions.explanation: A liquid flows because its particles can slide past each other, while a solid's particles only vibrate in fixed positions.

questions.question: Which state has particles that are the FARTHEST apart?

choices.D: They are all the same distance apart

questions.explanation: Gas particles are the farthest apart of the three states, which is why a gas can spread out to fill any space.

questions.question: A steel nail and a glass of water are compared. Which statement is correct?

choices.A: Both take the shape of their container
choices.B: The nail flows and the water does not
choices.C: Both spread out to fill a room
choices.D: The nail keeps its shape; the water takes the shape of the glass

questions.explanation: The nail is a solid and keeps its shape, while the water is a liquid and takes the shape of the glass.

questions.question: Water vapor is which state of water?

choices.D: It is not water at all

questions.explanation: Water vapor is the gas state of water; it is the same substance as ice and liquid water, only the particles are spread far apart.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a liquid?
questions.explanation: Orange juice flows and takes the shape of its cup while keeping its volume, so it is a liquid.

questions.question: More particle movement and more spacing between particles generally means the state is
questions.explanation: More particle movement and spacing means a less rigid state, moving from solid toward liquid toward gas.

questions.question: Which is NOT one of the three common states of matter described?
questions.explanation: Powder is not a separate state of matter; the three common states are solid, liquid, and gas.

questions.question: If a sample of matter has a fixed volume but takes the shape of any container, it must be a
questions.explanation: Fixed volume plus taking the container's shape is the unique combination that describes a liquid.

questions.question: A scientist says a sample 'fills its container completely and has no fixed shape or volume.' This sample is a
questions.explanation: Having no fixed shape or volume and filling the whole container describes a gas.

questions.question: Which statement about solids and liquids is TRUE?

choices.A: Both take the shape of their container
choices.B: Both have particles that zoom far apart
choices.C: Both keep a definite volume, but only the liquid takes the shape of its container

questions.explanation: Solids and liquids both have a definite volume, but only the liquid changes shape to match its container.

questions.question: Why does a gas spread out to fill its whole container?

choices.B: It has more particles than a solid
choices.C: Its particles only vibrate in place
choices.D: Its particles are far apart and zoom around freely

questions.explanation: Gas particles are far apart and move around freely, so they spread out to fill the entire container.

questions.question: Which everyday object is the best example of a solid?
questions.explanation: A metal key keeps its own shape and volume, making it a solid.

questions.question: As the same substance changes from solid to liquid to gas, what stays the same?

choices.C: The substance it is made of
choices.D: How spread out the particles are

questions.explanation: The substance stays the same through all three states; only the arrangement and motion of its particles change.

questions.question: A liquid is poured from a tall glass into a wide bowl. What happens to its volume?

choices.D: The volume stays the same, but the shape changes

questions.explanation: A liquid keeps its volume when moved to a new container; only its shape changes to match the bowl.

questions.question: Which list shows the states in order of INCREASING particle movement?
questions.explanation: Particles move least in a solid, more in a liquid, and most in a gas, so the order is solid, liquid, gas.

questions.question: Which observation BEST shows that air is a gas?

choices.A: It spreads out to completely fill a sealed jar
choices.B: It pours like water into a cup
choices.C: It keeps a fixed shape on a table
choices.D: It can be held in your hand as a block

questions.explanation: Air spreads out to completely fill a sealed jar, which shows it is a gas.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT true about the particles in a gas?

choices.B: They are packed tightly and only vibrate
choices.D: They spread out to fill a container

questions.explanation: Being packed tightly and only vibrating describes a solid's particles, not a gas's. Gas particles are far apart and move freely.

questions.question: A balloon and a brick of the same size are compared. The brick keeps its shape if you remove its container, but the gas in the balloon would spread out. This is because

choices.A: the brick is a gas and the balloon holds a solid
choices.C: the brick is a solid with tightly packed particles, while the gas has particles that spread freely
choices.D: gases always keep a fixed shape

questions.explanation: The brick is a solid with tightly packed particles that hold its shape, while the gas has free-moving particles that spread out.

questions.question: Which best describes the particles in a solid?

choices.B: Close together and sliding past each other
choices.C: Spread out to fill the container
choices.D: Packed tightly and vibrating in place

questions.explanation: Solid particles are packed tightly and vibrate in place, which is why a solid holds its shape.

questions.question: A puddle, a stone, and steam are observed. Which correctly identifies their states?

choices.A: Puddle = liquid, stone = solid, steam = gas
choices.B: Puddle = solid, stone = gas, steam = liquid
choices.C: Puddle = gas, stone = liquid, steam = solid

questions.explanation: A puddle is liquid water, a stone is a solid, and steam is water in the gas state.

questions.question: Which statement correctly compares all three states of matter?

choices.A: Solids and gases keep their shape, but liquids do not
choices.B: Gases keep their shape, while solids and liquids do not
choices.C: Solids keep shape and volume, liquids keep only volume, and gases keep neither
choices.D: All three states keep both shape and volume

questions.explanation: Solids keep both shape and volume, liquids keep volume but take the container's shape, and gases keep neither.

2-2.title: Changes of State
2-2.learn:
KEY IDEAS

Matter changes state when it gains or loses thermal energy (heat). The substance stays the SAME — only its state changes as particles speed up or slow down.

Adding heat (particles speed up):
- Melting: solid → liquid
- Evaporation/boiling: liquid → gas

Removing heat (particles slow down):
- Condensation: gas → liquid
- Freezing: liquid → solid

Example 1 — Ice cube on a warm day
Adding heat to ice makes its particles move faster until it melts into liquid water. More heat evaporates it into water vapor.

Example 2 — Cold glass 'sweating'
Water drops form on the outside of a cold glass when water vapor in the air loses heat and condenses (gas → liquid).

Example 3 — Freezing
Putting liquid water in a freezer removes heat. The particles slow down until the water freezes into solid ice.

questions.question: Changing a solid into a liquid by adding heat is called
questions.explanation: Melting is the change from solid to liquid when heat is added.

questions.question: Which change of state happens when a liquid turns into a gas?
questions.explanation: Evaporation (or boiling) is the change from liquid to gas as heat is added.

questions.question: When a gas loses heat and turns into a liquid, the process is called
questions.explanation: Condensation is the change from gas to liquid when heat is removed.

questions.question: Freezing is the change of state from
questions.explanation: Freezing is the change from liquid to solid as heat is removed.

questions.question: During a change of state, the substance itself
questions.explanation: A change of state is a physical change; the substance stays the same while only its state changes.

questions.question: Water drops appear on the outside of a cold soda can on a hot day. This is an example of
questions.explanation: Water vapor in the warm air loses heat to the cold can and condenses into liquid drops.

questions.question: Adding heat to a substance causes its particles to
questions.explanation: Adding heat (thermal energy) makes particles move faster and spread apart, which can change the state.

questions.question: Which two processes both require REMOVING heat?
questions.explanation: Condensation (gas to liquid) and freezing (liquid to solid) both happen when heat is removed.

questions.question: A puddle of water slowly disappears on a sunny day. What happened?
questions.explanation: The Sun's heat caused the liquid water to evaporate into invisible water vapor.

questions.question: A student heats ice until it melts, then keeps heating until it boils away. In order, the states are
questions.explanation: Heating ice melts the solid to liquid, then boils the liquid into gas: solid → liquid → gas.

questions.question: What must a substance gain or lose for its state to change?
questions.explanation: A substance changes state when it gains or loses thermal energy (heat), which speeds up or slows down its particles.

questions.question: Condensation is the change of state from
questions.explanation: Condensation is the change from gas to liquid, which happens when heat is removed.

questions.question: Removing heat from a substance causes its particles to

choices.C: move slower and come closer together

questions.explanation: Removing heat makes particles slow down and move closer together, which can change the state.

questions.question: Putting liquid water in a freezer turns it into ice. This change is called
questions.explanation: Freezing is the change from liquid to solid as heat is removed, so the water becomes ice.

questions.question: Which two processes both happen when heat is ADDED?
questions.explanation: Melting (solid to liquid) and evaporation (liquid to gas) both happen when heat is added.

questions.question: An ice cube left on a warm table turns into a small pool of water. This is
questions.explanation: Adding heat makes the ice particles move faster until the solid melts into liquid water.

questions.question: Which change of state is the OPPOSITE of melting?
questions.explanation: Melting goes solid to liquid by adding heat; freezing goes liquid to solid by removing heat, so freezing is the opposite.

questions.question: Which change of state is the OPPOSITE of evaporation?
questions.explanation: Evaporation goes liquid to gas by adding heat; condensation goes gas to liquid by removing heat, so condensation is the opposite.

questions.question: Dew forms on grass overnight as the air cools. This is an example of
questions.explanation: As the air cools, water vapor loses heat and condenses into liquid water droplets, forming dew.

questions.question: A change of state, such as ice melting, is best described as

choices.A: a chemical change that makes a new substance
choices.B: a physical change where the substance stays the same

questions.explanation: A change of state is a physical change; the substance stays the same while only its state changes.

questions.question: Wet clothes dry on a clothesline in the sun. Which change of state happened?
questions.explanation: The Sun's heat causes the liquid water in the clothes to evaporate into water vapor, drying the clothes.

questions.question: Which of these does NOT require adding heat?
questions.explanation: Freezing happens when heat is removed, not added. Melting, evaporation, and boiling all require adding heat.

questions.question: When water vapor turns into liquid drops on a cold mirror after a hot shower, the process is
questions.explanation: The water vapor loses heat to the cold mirror and condenses into liquid drops.

questions.question: During melting, the particles of the substance

choices.A: slow down and lock into place
choices.B: spread far apart and zoom freely
choices.C: gain energy and begin to slide past each other

questions.explanation: When a solid melts, its particles gain energy and begin to slide past each other, forming a liquid.

questions.question: Which sequence shows water LOSING heat the whole time?
questions.explanation: Going water vapor to liquid water to ice means heat is removed at each step (condensation then freezing).

questions.question: Frost forms on a cold window when water vapor turns directly into ice. This shows that a state change happens when the vapor
questions.explanation: Frost forms when water vapor loses heat, so removing thermal energy caused the change of state.

questions.question: A pot of water on a hot stove begins to boil, sending steam into the air. This change is
questions.explanation: Boiling is rapid evaporation; the heat turns the liquid water into water vapor (steam).

questions.question: Which statement about changes of state is TRUE?

choices.B: They happen as particles speed up or slow down with heat

questions.explanation: Changes of state happen as a substance's particles speed up or slow down when heat is added or removed.

questions.question: To change ice directly back and forth, melting turns ice to water and freezing turns water to ice. The difference between them is

choices.A: melting removes heat and freezing adds heat
choices.C: melting adds heat and freezing removes heat

questions.explanation: Melting adds heat to turn solid into liquid, while freezing removes heat to turn liquid into solid.

questions.question: A glass of ice water has drops forming on its OUTSIDE. Where did that water come from?

choices.C: The ice melted through the glass
choices.D: Water vapor in the air condensed on the cold glass

questions.explanation: The outside water is water vapor from the air that lost heat to the cold glass and condensed into liquid drops.

questions.question: Which change of state turns a gas into a liquid?
questions.explanation: Condensation is the change from gas to liquid when heat is removed.

questions.question: Which change of state turns a solid into a liquid?
questions.explanation: Melting is the change from solid to liquid when heat is added.

questions.question: A chocolate bar left in a hot car becomes soft and runny. The chocolate has
questions.explanation: Heat made the solid chocolate's particles move faster until it melted into a liquid.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT a change of state caused by removing heat?
questions.explanation: Melting happens when heat is added. Freezing, condensation, and frost forming all happen when heat is removed.

questions.question: As a substance freezes, its particles

choices.A: slow down and lock into fixed positions

questions.explanation: When a liquid freezes, its particles slow down and lock into fixed positions, forming a solid.

questions.question: Which pair of changes are opposites of each other?
questions.explanation: Melting (solid to liquid, heat added) and freezing (liquid to solid, heat removed) are opposite changes of state.

questions.question: When water vapor in clouds cools and turns into rain drops, the change of state is
questions.explanation: Cooling water vapor causes it to condense from a gas into liquid water drops, which can fall as rain.

questions.question: If you add heat to a block of ice for a long time, which order of states will you most likely see?
questions.explanation: Heating ice melts the solid to a liquid, then evaporates the liquid to a gas: solid, liquid, gas.

questions.question: During any change of state, the mass of the substance

choices.A: stays the same because it is the same substance

questions.explanation: Because a change of state is a physical change of the same substance, the matter is conserved and the mass stays the same.

questions.question: Which statement correctly pairs a process with its energy change?
questions.explanation: Freezing removes heat to change a liquid into a solid. Evaporation and melting add heat, and condensation also removes heat, so the correct pairing here is freezing removes heat.

2-3.title: Gas Behavior
2-3.learn:
KEY IDEAS

Gases act in special ways because their particles are far apart and move fast. Three properties are connected: volume (space), temperature (how fast particles move), and pressure (how hard particles push on the container).

Key relationships:
- Squeeze a gas into a SMALLER space → particles hit the walls more often → pressure goes UP.
- HEAT a gas → particles move faster and spread out → the gas expands or pushes harder (higher pressure if the space can't grow).
- COOL a gas → particles slow and move closer → the gas takes less space.

Example 1 — Balloon in heat and cold
A balloon EXPANDS in heat because the gas particles move faster and push outward. The same balloon SHRINKS in the cold because the particles slow and move closer.

Example 2 — Squeezing gas
Pushing a plunger to make a smaller space raises the gas pressure because the same particles crowd into less room and hit the walls more often.

Example 3 — Bike tire
A bike tire feels firmer on a hot day because the warm gas inside expands and pushes harder on the tire walls.

questions.question: Gas particles, compared to solid and liquid particles, are
questions.explanation: Gas particles are far apart and move fast, which gives gases their special behavior.

questions.question: If you squeeze a gas into a smaller space, its pressure usually
questions.explanation: Crowding the same particles into a smaller space makes them hit the walls more often, raising the pressure.

questions.question: What happens to gas particles when the gas is heated?

choices.B: They move faster and spread out

questions.explanation: Heating a gas gives its particles more energy, so they move faster and spread out.

questions.question: A balloon left in a hot car gets bigger. This is because the gas inside

choices.C: warmed up and its particles spread out

questions.explanation: Heat makes the gas particles move faster and spread out, so the balloon expands.

questions.question: A balloon placed in a freezer shrinks because the gas inside

choices.B: cooled down, so its particles slowed and moved closer

questions.explanation: Cooling slows the particles and lets them move closer together, so the balloon shrinks.

questions.question: Pressure in a gas is caused by

choices.B: particles hitting the walls of the container

questions.explanation: Gas pressure comes from the particles striking the walls of their container.

questions.question: A sealed, rigid container of gas is heated but cannot change size. The pressure inside will
questions.explanation: Heating makes the particles move faster and hit the walls harder and more often, so in a rigid container the pressure increases.

questions.question: Which change would make gas particles hit the container walls MORE often?

choices.B: Squeezing the gas into a smaller space
choices.D: Letting the gas expand into a bigger space

questions.explanation: Squeezing the gas into a smaller space crowds the particles so they hit the walls more often, raising the pressure.

questions.question: A bike tire feels firmer on a hot afternoon than on a cold morning. This is because the warm gas inside

choices.B: expanded and pushed harder on the tire

questions.explanation: Warm gas particles move faster and push harder on the tire walls, so the tire feels firmer.

questions.question: Which best summarizes how temperature affects a gas?

choices.B: Higher temperature makes particles faster, so the gas expands or pushes harder
choices.C: Temperature has no effect on gases
choices.D: Higher temperature turns gas into solid

questions.explanation: Raising the temperature speeds up the particles, causing the gas to expand or push harder on its container.

questions.question: Which three properties of a gas are connected to one another?
questions.explanation: A gas's volume, temperature, and pressure are connected properties that affect one another.

questions.question: In a gas, temperature is a measure of

choices.D: how many walls the container has

questions.explanation: Temperature is a measure of how fast the gas particles move; higher temperature means faster particles.

questions.question: Pressure in a gas describes

choices.C: how hard the particles push on the container

questions.explanation: Pressure is how hard the gas particles push on the walls of the container by hitting them.

questions.question: Cooling a gas causes its particles to

choices.D: slow down and move closer together

questions.explanation: Cooling a gas makes its particles slow down and move closer together, so the gas takes up less space.

questions.question: A balloon is moved from a warm room into a cold refrigerator. What most likely happens?
questions.explanation: In the cold the gas particles slow down and move closer together, so the balloon shrinks.

questions.question: Pushing a plunger to make the space inside a sealed syringe smaller will
questions.explanation: Squeezing the gas into a smaller space crowds the particles so they hit the walls more often, raising the pressure.

questions.question: Why does a gas expand when it is heated and free to grow?

choices.D: The particles move faster and push outward

questions.explanation: Heating makes the gas particles move faster and push outward, so the gas expands.

questions.question: Which change would make a gas take up LESS space?

choices.A: Heating it in a flexible balloon
choices.B: Cooling it in a flexible balloon

questions.explanation: Cooling a gas slows its particles and lets them move closer, so the gas takes up less space.

questions.question: A bike tire feels firmer on a hot day. This happens because the warm gas inside

choices.A: expanded and pushed harder on the tire walls

questions.explanation: Warm gas particles move faster and push harder on the tire walls, so the tire feels firmer.

questions.question: Which is NOT a property used to describe how a gas behaves?
questions.explanation: Volume, temperature, and pressure describe how a gas behaves; color is not one of these connected properties.

questions.question: If the space holding a gas gets bigger and nothing else changes, the particles will hit the walls
questions.explanation: In a larger space the same particles are more spread out, so they hit the walls less often and the pressure drops.

questions.question: A sealed metal can of gas is thrown into a fire. Because the can cannot grow, heating the gas will

choices.B: turn the gas into a solid
choices.C: keep the pressure exactly the same
choices.D: raise the pressure inside, possibly making it burst

questions.explanation: Heating speeds up the particles so they hit the rigid walls harder and more often, raising the pressure until the can may burst.

questions.question: What causes the particles of a gas to push on the walls of its container?

choices.A: The particles striking the walls as they move

questions.explanation: Gas pressure comes from the moving particles striking the walls of their container.

questions.question: Two identical balloons are filled with the same amount of gas. One sits in the sun and one sits in the shade. Which is larger?
questions.explanation: The warmer gas in the sun balloon has faster particles that spread out and push harder, so that balloon is larger.

questions.question: Which best explains why gas pressure goes UP when the gas is squeezed into a smaller space?

choices.B: The gas turns into a liquid
choices.D: The same number of particles hit the walls more often

questions.explanation: Squeezing crowds the same number of particles into less room, so they hit the walls more often and pressure rises.

questions.question: A gas is cooled inside a flexible container that can shrink. The volume of the gas will most likely
questions.explanation: Cooling slows the particles and lets them move closer, so a flexible container shrinks and the volume decreases.

questions.question: Which statement about gas particles is TRUE compared to liquid particles?

choices.A: Gas particles are far apart and move faster
choices.D: Gas particles are locked in a crystal

questions.explanation: Gas particles are far apart and move faster than liquid particles, which gives gases their special behavior.

questions.question: A scuba tank holds a lot of air squeezed into a small metal tank. The pressure inside is high because

choices.B: many particles are crowded into a small space and hit the walls often

questions.explanation: Crowding many particles into the small tank makes them hit the walls very often, creating high pressure.

questions.question: Which of these would lower the pressure of a gas in a flexible container?
questions.explanation: Cooling the gas slows the particles so they hit the walls less hard and less often, lowering the pressure.

questions.question: When a gas is heated, the speed of its particles
questions.explanation: Heating a gas adds energy, so the speed of its particles increases.

questions.question: A partly flat football is left in the hot sun and becomes firmer. The best explanation is that the gas inside

choices.A: warmed up, so its particles moved faster and pushed harder

questions.explanation: The warm gas particles move faster and push harder on the football walls, making it feel firmer.

questions.question: Which is NOT a way to increase the pressure of a gas?

choices.A: Squeezing it into a smaller space
choices.B: Heating it in a rigid container
choices.D: Adding more gas to the same container

questions.explanation: Cooling a gas slows its particles and lowers pressure. Squeezing, heating in a rigid container, or adding gas all raise pressure.

questions.question: Which everyday example best shows a gas expanding when heated?

choices.B: An ice cube melting on a plate
choices.C: A rock staying the same on a table
choices.D: A balloon swelling larger after being left in a hot car

questions.explanation: A balloon swelling larger in the heat shows the gas expanding as its particles move faster and spread out.

questions.question: How does squeezing a gas into a smaller space affect how often particles hit the walls?

choices.A: They hit the walls less often
choices.B: They hit the walls more often

questions.explanation: In a smaller space the particles are crowded closer to the walls, so they hit the walls more often.

questions.question: A balloon expands in summer heat and shrinks in winter cold. This shows that gas volume

choices.A: increases when the gas is heated and decreases when it is cooled
choices.C: decreases when the gas is heated

questions.explanation: Heating makes the gas expand and cooling makes it shrink, so the volume increases with heat and decreases with cold.

questions.question: Which best describes what happens to gas pressure in a rigid, sealed container as the gas cools?

choices.D: The gas becomes a solid immediately

questions.explanation: Cooling slows the particles so they hit the rigid walls less hard and less often, so the pressure falls.

questions.question: Why can a gas be squeezed into a much smaller space, while a solid cannot?

choices.C: A gas has lots of empty space between its far-apart particles

questions.explanation: Because gas particles are far apart with lots of empty space between them, a gas can be squeezed into a smaller space.

questions.question: Which action increases the speed of gas particles AND can make the gas push harder?
questions.explanation: Heating the gas speeds up the particles, which makes them push harder on the container.

questions.question: A sealed syringe of air is pushed in halfway, then released. The plunger springs back out. This shows that the squeezed gas had
